concepts.title: Order of operations
concepts.handExample: Compare 2 + 3 × 4 with (2 + 3) × 4.

concepts.title: Fractions and ratios
concepts.handExample: Simplify 6/8 and compare 3:4 with 6:8.

concepts.title: Percentages and percentage points
concepts.handExample: Distinguish a rise from 40% to 50% from a 10% relative increase.

concepts.title: Powers and roots
concepts.handExample: Calculate 3² and √9; distinguish √9 from solving x² = 9.

concepts.title: Absolute value
concepts.handExample: Compare signed error −3 with its magnitude 3.

concepts.title: Substitution and evaluating expressions
concepts.handExample: Evaluate 2x + y at x = 3, y = −1.

concepts.title: Solving an equation
concepts.handExample: Undo the operations in 2x + 3 = 11.

concepts.title: Inequalities and intervals
concepts.handExample: Mark the inputs satisfying −1 ≤ x < 2.

concepts.title: Sets and membership
concepts.handExample: Find the intersection of {1, 2, 3} and {2, 4}.

concepts.title: Coordinates and graphs
concepts.handExample: Plot (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6), naming both axes.

concepts.title: Domain and range
concepts.handExample: Find the allowed inputs and possible outputs of √x over real numbers.

concepts.title: Slope and intercept
concepts.handExample: Find the slope between (1, 3) and (3, 7), then the intercept.

concepts.title: Function composition
concepts.handExample: For f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 1, compare f(g(3)) and g(f(3)).

concepts.title: Inverse functions
concepts.handExample: Undo f(x) = 3x + 2; explain why an inverse needs a suitable domain.

concepts.title: Piecewise functions
concepts.handExample: Evaluate a rule using one formula below zero and another above it.

concepts.title: Polynomials
concepts.handExample: Evaluate x² + 2x + 1 at three inputs and identify its degree.

concepts.title: Means and weighted averages
concepts.handExample: Compare an equal average of 2 and 8 with weights 3/4 and 1/4.

concepts.title: Angles and radians
concepts.handExample: Relate a quarter turn to 90° and π/2 radians.

concepts.title: Sine and cosine
concepts.handExample: Read the coordinates of a point on the unit circle at quarter turns.

concepts.title: Polar coordinates
concepts.handExample: Represent (0, 2) using a length and an angle.

concepts.title: Norms and unit vectors
concepts.handExample: Turn (3, 4) into a unit vector; distinguish length from direction.

concepts.title: Orthogonality
concepts.handExample: Check that (1, 1) and (1, −1) have zero dot product.

concepts.title: Vector projection
concepts.handExample: Project (3, 4) onto the horizontal axis and calculate the residual.

concepts.title: Span
concepts.handExample: Identify which points multiples of (1, 2) can reach.

concepts.title: Linear independence
concepts.handExample: Decide whether (1, 2) and (2, 4) provide two independent directions.

concepts.title: Basis and dimension

concepts.title: Systems of linear equations
concepts.handExample: Solve x + y = 5 and x − y = 1.

concepts.title: Gaussian elimination
concepts.handExample: Remove one variable by subtracting rows in a two-equation system.

concepts.title: Matrix inverse
concepts.handExample: Undo a diagonal scaling; contrast it with a transformation that discards a coordinate. Define the identity matrix explicitly here.

concepts.title: Matrix rank
concepts.handExample: Compare the independent columns of [[1, 2], [2, 4]] and the identity matrix.

concepts.title: Low-rank approximation
concepts.handExample: Replace diag(4, 1) with diag(4, 0) and measure squared entrywise error.

concepts.title: Average rate of change
concepts.handExample: Compute the slope of x² between x = 1 and x = 2.

concepts.title: Limits
concepts.handExample: Examine (x² − 1)/(x − 1) near x = 1, distinguishing its limit from its undefined value there.

concepts.title: Finite differences
concepts.handExample: Approximate the derivative of x² at x = 2 with two different step sizes.

concepts.title: Local linear approximation
concepts.handExample: Use the slope of x² at 2 to estimate 2.1² and compare with the exact answer.

concepts.title: Functions of several variables
concepts.handExample: Evaluate f(x, y) = x² + 3y at two input pairs.

concepts.title: Partial derivatives
concepts.handExample: For x² + 3y², vary x while holding y fixed, then reverse the roles.

concepts.title: Jacobian
concepts.handExample: Build the derivative matrix for F(x, y) = (2x + y, x − y).

concepts.title: Convexity
concepts.handExample: Compare a bowl-shaped objective with a two-valley objective.

concepts.title: Constraints and feasible regions
concepts.handExample: Draw the allowed region x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 4.

concepts.title: Learning rate and convergence
concepts.handExample: Take one gradient step on (x − 3)² with step sizes 0.25, 0.5 and 1.

concepts.title: Random variables
concepts.handExample: Map two coin tosses to the number of heads.

concepts.title: Discrete probability distributions
concepts.handExample: Build the probability table for that head count and check its total.

concepts.title: Bernoulli distribution
concepts.handExample: Represent a single success/failure trial with success probability 1/4.

concepts.title: Binomial distribution
concepts.handExample: Enumerate three fair tosses and find the probability of exactly two heads.

concepts.title: Joint probability
concepts.handExample: Fill a 2 × 2 table for two binary outcomes.

concepts.title: Marginalization
concepts.handExample: Sum that table's rows and columns to recover individual distributions.

concepts.title: Independence
concepts.handExample: Test whether a joint probability equals the product of its marginals.

concepts.title: Conditional independence
concepts.handExample: Use a small supplied table to see whether two variables are independent within each group.

concepts.title: Likelihood
concepts.handExample: Compare how well coin biases 1/2 and 3/4 explain two heads and one tail.

concepts.title: Probability density
concepts.handExample: Use a uniform density over [0, 2] to calculate probability from area.

concepts.title: Normal distribution
concepts.handExample: Locate values one standard deviation from a stated mean; use supplied areas rather than unexplained tables.

concepts.title: Cumulative probability
concepts.handExample: Add a discrete table's probabilities up to a chosen threshold.

concepts.title: Populations and samples
concepts.handExample: Enumerate all size-two samples from a four-item population.

concepts.title: Median and quantiles
concepts.handExample: Sort five values and compare the median with the mean after adding an outlier.

concepts.title: Sample variance
concepts.handExample: Calculate squared deviations for three readings; explain the estimator and denominator being used.

concepts.title: Sampling and selection bias
concepts.handExample: Compare an average from all four readings with an average after selecting only high readings.

concepts.title: Law of large numbers
concepts.handExample: Follow the running head fraction in a supplied sequence of coin tosses.

concepts.handExample: Build the distribution of sample means from a small population; explain the conditions and approximation limits.

concepts.title: Standard error
concepts.handExample: Distinguish spread of observations from spread of sample means using enumerated samples.

concepts.handExample: Interpret intervals from repeated supplied samples without claiming a frequentist interval assigns probability to a fixed parameter.

concepts.title: Randomized experiments
concepts.handExample: Compare group mean outcomes and explain why random assignment matters.

concepts.title: Baseline models
concepts.handExample: Compare always predicting the majority class or training mean with a learned model.

concepts.title: Cross-validation
concepts.handExample: Rotate three held-out folds while fitting preprocessing only on each training fold.

concepts.title: One-hot encoding
concepts.handExample: Encode three categories without inventing an ordinal relationship.

concepts.title: Feature engineering

concepts.title: Mean absolute error
concepts.handExample: Compare absolute and squared losses on errors 1, 1 and 4.

concepts.title: Hyperparameter search
concepts.handExample: Choose among a supplied validation-results table while leaving test results untouched.

concepts.title: Learning curves
concepts.handExample: Read training and validation errors as the number of examples grows.

concepts.title: Bias–variance tradeoff
concepts.handExample: Compare predictions from several fits across repeated supplied training sets.

concepts.title: Unsupervised learning
concepts.handExample: Group unlabeled points, then distinguish the grouping from known target labels.

concepts.title: k-means clustering
concepts.handExample: Assign four one-dimensional points to two centers and update their means once.

concepts.title: Entropy
concepts.handExample: Compare uncertainty in a fair binary outcome with a certain outcome, using base-two logarithms.

concepts.title: Mutual information
concepts.handExample: Compare independent bits with two identical bits using tiny probability tables.

concepts.title: Maximum likelihood estimation
concepts.handExample: Find the coin bias maximizing the likelihood of two heads in three tosses.

concepts.title: Maximum a posteriori estimation
concepts.handExample: Combine a supplied likelihood and prior table over three candidate parameters.

concepts.title: Logistic regression
concepts.handExample: Convert a linear score into a probability, then distinguish the probability from the chosen class.

concepts.title: Naive Bayes

concepts.title: Kernel methods
concepts.handExample: Compare an explicit small feature map with the dot products it produces.

concepts.title: Confusion matrix
concepts.handExample: Classify six predictions into true/false positives and negatives.

concepts.title: Decision thresholds
concepts.handExample: Move a threshold across those six scores and recount mistakes.

concepts.title: Precision–recall curves
concepts.handExample: Compute precision and recall at three thresholds.

concepts.title: ROC curves and AUC
concepts.handExample: Count how often a positive example ranks above a negative, handling ties explicitly.

concepts.title: Complex numbers
concepts.handExample: Add 2 + 3i and 1 − i; plot the result in the complex plane.

concepts.title: Complex multiplication and rotation

concepts.title: Euler's formula
concepts.handExample: Relate e^(iθ) to quarter turns using cosine and sine.

concepts.title: Amplitude and phase
concepts.handExample: Compare two waves of equal frequency with different heights or horizontal shifts.

concepts.title: Superposition of signals
concepts.handExample: Add two short sampled waves entry by entry.

concepts.title: Sampling and aliasing
concepts.handExample: Sample two different waves at the same four times and observe identical samples.

concepts.title: Fourier transform and the DFT
concepts.handExample: Transform the four samples [1, 0, −1, 0], with the transform convention stated.

concepts.title: Algorithmic complexity
concepts.handExample: Count operations as a small input doubles; distinguish growth rates from measured runtime.

concepts.title: Fast Fourier Transform
concepts.handExample: Split a four-point DFT into even and odd parts and count reused calculations.

concepts.title: Spectrograms

concepts.title: Computation graphs
concepts.handExample: Draw the operations for (wx + b)² and identify reused intermediate values.

concepts.title: Tensor reshaping

concepts.title: Weight initialization
concepts.handExample: Show why two identically initialized hidden neurons can receive identical updates.

concepts.title: Vanishing and exploding gradients
concepts.handExample: Multiply four local derivatives of 1/2 or 2 and inspect the resulting sensitivity.

concepts.title: Gradient clipping
concepts.handExample: Clip a two-dimensional gradient to a stated maximum norm.

concepts.title: Momentum
concepts.handExample: Apply a stated recurrence to three supplied gradients.

concepts.title: Adam
concepts.handExample: Compute its first update from a scalar gradient with all conventions and bias corrections supplied.

concepts.title: Dropout

concepts.title: Residual connections

concepts.title: Graphs and adjacency matrices
concepts.handExample: Convert a three-node drawing into a matrix and count neighbors.

concepts.title: Byte-pair tokenization

concepts.title: Rotary positional embeddings
concepts.handExample: Rotate a pair of coordinates at two positions and examine their relative angle.

concepts.title: Feed-forward blocks
concepts.handExample: Apply two small linear maps with a nonlinearity between them to one token vector.

Temperature and sampling

concepts.title: Top-k and top-p sampling

concepts.handExample: Compare two models' probabilities for a three-token sequence.

concepts.title: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA)

concepts.title: Temporal-difference learning
concepts.handExample: Calculate one reward-plus-next-value prediction error and update a value estimate.
